correctness.rationale: For each length-three window, unscaled MAD equals min(|d_i|,|d_{i+1}|,|d_i+d_{i+1}|). Each coordinate section of that map is 1-Lipschitz, so changing one input difference can change at most its two incident output coordinates by at most the input change. The weighted variation column bound is v_{j-2}+2v_{j-1}+v_j for interior edges, with the stated boundary values. Coordinate telescoping proves the all-pair upper bound. Strict rational local triples (-3/2,1,-3) and perturbation 1/10 attain alpha=-epsilon,beta=+epsilon simultaneously; boundary triples (1,3)/(3,1) attain the endpoint ratios. Hence each column ratio and their maximum is attained by finite real pairs. Exact rational checker corroborates the identity, witness quotients, arbitrary-weight inequalities, and all unweighted regimes.

originality.rationale: Both complete primary scientific texts that define/use the local MAD were compared at the level of operator and theorem: Rousseeuw--Croux treats scale, influence and breakdown; Pearson et al. treats Hampel replacement and replication-weighted median windows. Neither gives any exact two-input weighted path-variation coefficient. Indexed scientific results on running medians and min/max morphology act on other quantities and do not subsume this simultaneously weighted local MAD output formula. The exact 2,3,4 onset and sharp edge-weight criterion were not found in the inspected sources. Historical equivalence remains possible outside the inspected corpus.

value.rationale: Local MAD is the robust scale used by Hampel outlier screening. A high breakdown point does not control path-variation amplification between two moving-scale estimates. This all-length theorem resolves the exact worst-case perturbation budget for every positive pair of input/output edge-weight sequences, provides an iff nonexpansivity criterion, identifies the first unstable signal length and saturated gain, and supplies actual worst-case signals. It is a complete natural classification at the smallest nontrivial robust-scale window, not merely a one-off computation or normalized rewriting of running-median/standard-deviation bounds.
